Top items we need clarified for our internal review:

Natalie — thanks for the clear notes and the diagram. Looping in Vivek (networking/ops) to annotate the control/data boundaries and confirm egress patterns.

Preliminary answers:
- Control plane: we recommend placing the Redwood control plane endpoints in a dedicated management subnet with restricted ingress (customer CIDR + Redwood peering CIDRs only). Control traffic is TLS over mutual auth; we can configure customer-managed TLS termination if required.
- Data plane (inference workers): keep in private subnets with no public IPs. For model pulls and telemetry we support three egress patterns:
  1) Customer-managed NAT gateway/TGW (recommended for strict egress control)
  2) Customer HTTP proxy (corporate outbound proxy) — Redwood can be configured to route downloads via that proxy
  3) Redwood-managed egress via cross-account VPC endpoint with strict allowlist (falls back to option 1 for highly regulated customers)
- Logs/backups: we support direct push to customer S3 via signed STS role (preferred). As a fallback, Redwood-managed storage with cross-account replication can be used but will require a documented data-handling SLA.

I'll attach a compact boundary mapping (controlplane-dataflow-drawio.png) and a deployment checklist (deployment-checklist.xlsx) that mirrors what your security team will want. Vivek — can you add notes on required SG rules and recommended flow logs?

I can also run a 30-minute call this week to walk the checklist with Samir / your infra folks.

Best,

Natalie / team — quick notes from the ops side after reviewing the diagram:

1) Control plane placement:
- Put control-plane API endpoints into a management VPC subnet with no routes to the public internet. Control-plane actors (Redwood control services) should be able to reach your KMS endpoint (if using customer KMS) and the STS endpoint. If you restrict egress, please add the minimal set of endpoints we provide in the checklist.

2) Security groups / flow rules (summary):
- Control plane SG: allow inbound from your admin CIDR on 443; allow outbound to KMS/S3 STS endpoints.
- Data plane SG: allow inbound only from internal load balancer subnets and from model storage endpoints; ephemeral outbound to your proxy or NAT.

3) Egress for model downloads:
- If you use a NAT/Gateway, use a dedicated route table for the inference subnets so we can pin egress to the right address range for allowlists.
- If you prefer an HTTP proxy, ensure the proxy exposes TLS inspection exceptions for our model tar downloads (we sign packages).

4) Audit / flow logs:
- Enable VPC Flow Logs for both management and inference subnets (send to a central logging account).
- We will ship application-level audit events to your S3 via STS role; please confirm retention policy so we can align retention tags.

5) High-availability placement:
- Recommend spread inference workers across 3 AZs with per-AZ autoscaling to meet SLOs.

I'll markup the attached PNG with port/route annotations and return it by Monday. If you want, we can also add a small diagram showing fallback routing for model pulls (NAT -> proxy -> Redwood egress).

-Vivek
